title: Piano Roll Tricks
intro: The Piano Roll is where MIDI becomes music. Most people use about ten percent of it. Here is the rest.

tips.t: Select all notes of the same pitch in one click
tips.d: Click a key on the keyboard graphic at the left of the Piano Roll and every note at that pitch in the region is selected. Perfect for grabbing all the hi‑hats at once.

tips.t: Select similar notes with Edit > Select > Same Note Pitch
tips.d: Works across the whole region and respects your current selection as the reference.

tips.t: Select all following notes
tips.d: Edit > Select > All Following selects every note from the current selection to the end of the region. Ideal for transposing the back half of a part.

tips.t: Rubber‑band select without hitting notes
tips.d: Drag in empty space to lasso notes. Hold ⇧ to add to the existing selection rather than replacing it.

tips.t: Use Select > Inside Locators to grab a bar range
tips.d: Set the locators, then select only the notes inside them. Precise, repeatable, no mouse accuracy required.

tips.t: Nudge notes by tick with ⌥ and the arrow keys
tips.d: Set your nudge value in Edit > Move, then ⌥← and ⌥→ move the selection by exactly that amount. Groove work without the mouse.

tips.t: Change note length numerically in the inspector
tips.d: The event inspector at the top left shows position, pitch, velocity, length and channel for the selection. Type a value and every selected note updates at once.

tips.t: Type one length and every selected note follows
tips.d: Select the notes and type a length in the event inspector — they all take it. Force Legato is a different job: it stretches each note to meet the next, which is not the same as equal lengths.

tips.t: Force legato to fix gappy pads
tips.d: Piano Roll Edit > Trim > Note Force Legato extends every note to meet the next. Pads and basslines stop sounding stuttery instantly.

tips.t: Trim overlaps automatically
tips.d: Piano Roll Edit > Trim > Note Overlaps cleans up doubled notes that cause phasing and stuck voices on hardware.

tips.t: ⌥‑drag a note to duplicate it
tips.d: Hold ⌥ while dragging any note or selection to copy rather than move. Hold ⇧ too and it stays on the same pitch.

tips.t: Place a note between grid divisions
tips.d: Set Snap to a finer division, or switch Snap off for the drag. Do not reach for ⌃⌥-drag here — that gesture is drag-zoom, and using it will move your view instead of your note.

tips.t: Change velocity by dragging with the Velocity tool
tips.d: Pick the Velocity tool from the tool menu and drag up or down on a note. The note colour updates live and you never leave the Piano Roll.

tips.t: Draw a velocity ramp across a selection
tips.d: Select a run of notes, then draw a line across the velocity lane with the Pointer or the Pencil. Hold ⌘ while you do it to keep the relative differences between notes.

tips.t: Scale velocities rather than replacing them
tips.d: Typing a velocity value flattens everything to the same number. Instead, drag the velocity of one note in a selection and the others move relatively, preserving the performance.

tips.t: Show the automation lane inside the Piano Roll
tips.d: Press A with the Piano Roll focused to reveal MIDI CC lanes underneath the notes. Modwheel, expression and sustain edit right next to the notes they affect.

tips.t: Colour notes by velocity to read dynamics instantly
tips.d: In the Piano Roll's View menu, set note colour to Velocity. Flat parts become visibly, obviously flat.

tips.t: Quantise from the region inspector, not destructively
tips.d: The Quantize field in the Region inspector is non‑destructive and can be dialled back or removed at any point. Use it before you ever use the destructive version.

tips.t: Use Q‑Strength to keep the human feel
tips.d: Under the region's more‑options triangle, Q‑Strength at 60 to 80 percent pulls notes toward the grid without gluing them to it.

tips.t: Quantise only the notes that need it
tips.d: Select the offending notes in the Piano Roll and quantise the selection rather than the whole region. The good parts of the take stay untouched.

tips.t: Use Q‑Range to leave close notes alone
tips.d: Q‑Range quantises only notes that are further from the grid than a set amount, so a naturally tight performance is left alone while the strays get pulled in.
